ground_truth.unit: change in the probability of believing one does not lose (0/1 outcome)
ground_truth.context: Table 4 ("Effect of Feedback on Belief of Winning"), column (1), the paper's main specification (equation 2), a regression discontinuity in the respondent-specific estimated net gain from the tax and dividend policy.  Among respondents who received the customized win/lose feedback, restricted to those whose estimated net gain is within EUR 50 per year of zero: a linear probability model of the belief after feedback (1 if the respondent believes they do not lose, 0 if they believe they lose) on the predicted-winner indicator (the win feedback, which switches on when the estimated net gain exceeds zero), a quadratic in the estimated net gain, initial acceptance of the tax and dividend, and controls for incomes (piecewise continuous), socio-demographics and other motives.  This is the coefficient on the predicted-winner indicator.

As coded: 0.272 (0.059) (row 6656); no covariates 0.241 (0.056). rdrobust variants (DP58 Table 3, rows 6631-6690): conventional 0.157-0.282, bias-corrected 0.131-0.287; the misclassified respondents dropped (col 6) 0.282 (0.069).

ground_truth.context: Table 6 ("Effect of Self-Interest on Acceptance"), column (1), the paper's main self-interest estimate: two-stage least squares of acceptance of the tax and targeted dividend ("Yes" or "Don't know" to supporting it) on the belief that one does not lose from it, instrumented by the respondent's and the second adult's random eligibility for the targeted dividend (eligibility thresholds at the 20th, 30th, 40th or 50th income percentile, randomly assigned) and their interaction (first stage: Table 5 column 1), controlling for fixed effects for the policy assigned, a single-adult indicator, initial acceptance of the tax and dividend, incomes (piecewise linear with kinks at the 20th and 70th percentiles), estimated gains, socio-demographics and other motives. All respondents.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: The online-appendix control lists are unavailable. Controls were rebuilt from the data. Sociodemographics: sex, age bracket, employment status, CSP, education (4 levels), agglomeration size, region, household size, number aged 14+, left-right placement, smoker, main news source. Other motives: belief in environmental effectiveness and in progressivity. Incomes: continuous piecewise-linear terms in both adults' income percentiles with kinks at p20 and p70. Estimated gains: quadratic in the estimated net gain per consumption unit.

Estimated net gain = simule_gain (EUR/yr per consumption unit). Predicted winner = simule_gagnant, the displayed feedback; it differs from 1{simule_gain>0} for 56 respondents, 52 of them inside the |gain|<50 band.

Table 8: the progressivity belief is left out of the other-motive controls. It was only elicited in the survey wave that also received the effectiveness information (apres_modifs), so it is collinear with the instrument. The other-motive control there is the initial win/lose category.
Yellow Vests supporter = Gilets_jaunes in {soutient, est_dedans}. The initial win/lose belief G = initial category not 'Loser'. Column 3 also controls for the 3-level initial category.

Table 6 col 1 subsample = at least one adult's income percentile in [10,60] (both percentile variables as provided; 1,969 respondents). Eligibility instruments are traite_cible, traite_cible_conjoint and their product. Controls add policy-threshold fixed effects, a single-adult indicator and initial acceptance.

Table 8 instruments: apres_modifs = info on the scientific consensus about effectiveness (identified by its effect on the effectiveness belief) and info_CC. Strict definitions: approval = 'Oui', effective = 'Oui'.
Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors (coefficients do not depend on this).
deviations_stdout: control lists (online appendix) unavailable; sociodemo/other-motive/income controls reconstructed from variable names; heteroskedasticity-robust SEs.
Table 8 other-motive controls = initial win/lose category only (progressivity belief omitted: its missingness coincides with the E.E. information wave, collinear with the instrument).
cell.notes: Data: the object s (3,002 respondents) from code/after_preparation.RData. memisc S4 columns were converted to base vectors because memisc is not installed. No scripts, logs or result files in the package were opened. Attempts 1-5 were exploratory and printed no RESULT lines. Attempts 2 and 3 crashed while converting the memisc columns. Before its final completed run, attempt 3 also hit Docker infrastructure failures: a 'Transport endpoint is not connected' mount error, hung containers stuck in 'Created', and a daemon crash. Docker Desktop was restarted and the identical script then ran. Attempt 6 was the first scored run. Its collinearity warning showed that the progressivity 'not asked' level was collinear with the effectiveness-information instrument, which collapsed the Table 8 first stage (F = 1.5). The final run drops that control from Table 8 only (first-stage F = 10.9). No paper values were consulted or compared. Paper numbers used were sample-description counts only: 1,968 feedback recipients and 1,969 respondents in the [p10;p60] subsample, both matched by construction.
